entries.title: How much extra was each feature worth?
entries.caption: Extra payment estimate · VND millions · 95% intervals.
entries.source: Latent class estimates in the project materials; interval values retained from the existing model record.
notes: Both range intervals lie above zero. The larger point estimate in the design-sensitive group is not, by itself, a tested difference between groups.
The utility-focused interval crosses zero, while the design-sensitive interval stays positive. Read each group's uncertainty before using the point estimate.
The network premium is uncertain in the utility-focused group. The design-sensitive estimate has a positive reported interval.
Both design intervals cross zero. A positive point estimate alone gives a weak basis for setting a design premium.
method: Compare cars
Participants repeatedly chose between cars with different features and prices.
Look for patterns
Multinomial logit describes shared preferences. Mixed logit allows individual differences. Latent class looks for groups of buyers.
Estimate feature values
Willingness to pay (WTP) is the estimated extra amount for a feature. The displayed estimates come from the two-group model.
entries.equationNote: Feature units and price coding determine the resulting WTP unit. Cross-group differences need their own uncertainty calculation.

entries.title: The largest group contains 43.7% of reviews.
entries.caption: Reviews by group · largest is 43.7%.
entries.source: Project materials: 74,896 Booking.com reviews, 458 hotels, 10 reported groups.
notes: The largest group accounts for 43.7% of the review sample. Its share describes the cluster size; the attribute map is needed to understand what the group says.
Gastronomy is a reported cluster label. Use the original attribute analysis to inspect the pattern behind the name.
The label describes a profile interpretation. It does not assign a measured travel motive to every reviewer.
Read the sentiment and attribute pattern alongside this group label before choosing a service response.
A smaller cluster can still have a distinct service pattern. Its share is not a spending estimate.
The profile summarizes review features. It does not establish demographic or household characteristics.
Service design should follow the recorded attribute pattern rather than the cluster name alone.
The group label is a concise interpretation of room-related review patterns.
The share describes the sample partition. A price-sensitivity coefficient is not supplied for this cluster.
The profile is a review-based group; it does not identify verified local or repeat guests.

images.label: Attribute sentiment
images.note: Each row is an original numeric cluster ID; columns are hotel attributes. The source does not provide a checked crosswalk from these IDs to the named profiles, so the two label systems are kept separate.

images.label: Review volume
images.note: Original weekly review-volume figure by source market. The image reports a time pattern; counts have not been reconstructed from its pixels.

method: Read the comments
The materials report 108,906 sentences and 148,846 pairs linking a hotel attribute with a sentence.
Describe the feedback
Record which part of a stay is discussed and whether the comment is positive or negative.
Group similar patterns
K-means groups similar review patterns. A Gaussian mixture model (GMM) provides another way to check the grouping.
entries.equation: Review text → attribute features → clustering → profile interpretation
entries.equationNote: Sentiment and salience answer different questions: how an attribute is evaluated and how much it is mentioned.

entries.title: Cleanliness complaints had the largest downside.
entries.caption: Review language and hotel ratings.
entries.source: Reported PRCA coefficients from the project figure; OLS with HC1 robust standard errors.
notes: Cleanliness has a large downside coefficient and a much smaller upside coefficient. The asymmetry makes failure prevention the practical priority.
WiFi has a negative penalty and a slightly negative reward estimate. Keep that sign visible; a positive sentiment indicator does not guarantee a positive coefficient.
Staff service combines a substantial penalty with the largest positive reward estimate in the figure.
Room quality has a larger negative coefficient than its positive reward estimate. Service consistency matters before upgrades.
The estimated value coefficients suggest a larger downside than upside in this specification.
Location is classified as performance in the project materials, despite a small positive reward estimate.
Facilities have a stronger positive reward than negative penalty in this specification.
Food has a positive reward of 0.525 and a smaller negative penalty of −0.158.
method: Sort the comments
Sentence-BERT, a text-analysis model, matches sentences to eight hotel service attributes.
Compare praise and complaints
Examine positive and negative comments separately to see how each relates to review scores.
Interpret the pattern
The reported categories distinguish expected basics, services where better performance helps, and extras that can delight guests.
entries.equation: Rating = intercept + Σ penaltyj · negativej + Σ rewardj · positivej + error
entries.equationNote: Coefficients describe the supplied regression specification. The figure does not supply confidence intervals or a return-on-investment estimate.

entries.title: Four posts test two things separately.
entries.caption: 2 × 2 experiment · message strength × creator appeal.

items.label: Strong argument / high appeal
items.note: Both experimental dimensions are high. Compare with the other high-appeal cell to isolate the argument-quality contrast.

items.label: Weak argument / high appeal
items.note: Peripheral appeal is high while argument quality is weak. The message contrast should hold the appeal condition fixed.

items.label: Strong argument / low appeal
items.note: Argument quality is strong while appeal is low. Compare with the strong-argument, high-appeal condition for the appeal contrast.

items.label: Weak argument / low appeal
items.note: Both dimensions are low. This is one experimental condition; it is not a group defined by speciesism.

method: Change the message
Show a stronger or weaker product argument.
Change the creator cues
Vary the creator’s appeal. The study also examines attractiveness and similarity of attitudes.
Check audience preferences
Preference for human endorsers, called speciesism in this study, is measured separately. It is not an assigned post version.
entries.equation: Argument quality × peripheral appeal → purchase intention
entries.equationNote: The publication reports peripheral-cue relationships and moderation. Cell means and interaction coefficients are not supplied here.

entries.title: Basic food advice was better understood than calories.
entries.caption: Knowledge scores · food groups · diet associations.
entries.source: FCBEM paper: Table 2 (knowledge), Table 3 (diet) and Table 5 (regression); n = 280.

diet.label: Foods to limit
diet.direction: More groups to limit; higher is not healthier

method: Ask about food knowledge
The adapted CoNKS questionnaire has 20 questions: 7, 7 and 6 across its three topic areas.
Ask about activity and diet
IPAQ-SF is a short physical-activity questionnaire. DQQ asks about 29 food groups.
Compare the answers
The analysis checks how the answers vary together while accounting for age, sex, knowledge and activity. The reported model fit is R² = 0.538.
entries.equationNote: Coefficients are in the units shown, not comparable standardized effects. The paper rounds the activity interval to [0.003, 0.003]; its precision cannot be recovered from the printed table.

entries.title: Compare the restrictions with the support offered.
entries.caption: Estimated monthly value by policy feature.
entries.source: Existing CIEMB manuscript-table reconstruction: Table 5 values; Table 4 interactions.
method: Compare packages
Policy packages vary restrictions, public transport, financial support and governance.
Look for differences
Mixed logit allows preferences to vary across people. Additional comparisons examine differences between respondents.
Express the trade-off
Willingness to pay (WTP) converts a feature’s estimated value into a monthly amount. It is not a proposed government budget.
entries.equation: Utility = policy-attribute terms + respondent interactions + random component
entries.equationNote: An interaction changes how an attribute relates to preference. It is not an independent policy benefit to add to the package.

entries.title: Healthier-first menus changed two kinds of choice.
entries.caption: Planned calories · premium-tier choice.
entries.source: Project materials: Study 1 n = 257; Study 2 n = 147; ordinal logit and mediation.
method: Change the order
Show food options or price tiers in different orders.
Compare the choices
An ordinal logit model examines the choice of higher-priced tiers in Study 2.
Examine perceived value
The analysis examines whether people’s sense of value helps explain the choice. The reported indirect effect is −0.339, CI [−0.56, −0.15].
entries.equation: Menu condition → perceived value → tier choice
entries.equationNote: The mediation model helps interpret the trade-off. The odds ratio of 0.52 means lower odds, not a 48 percentage-point fall in probability.

entries.title: Engagement links content experience with returning.
entries.caption: Survey model · engagement and retention.
entries.source: Manuscript structure and reported figure; total n = 565, EFA = 200, CFA/SEM = 365.

inputs.label: Content experience
inputs.note: Content experience is a measured antecedent of engagement. EFA and CFA establish the scale structure before SEM estimates the structural relationships.

inputs.label: Expectation alignment
inputs.note: Expectation alignment is modeled separately from content experience. Its relationship with retention is examined through engagement.

inputs.label: Brand equity transfer
inputs.note: The brand-related construct enters the engagement model. A structural association does not assign a measured return on influencer spending.

method: Explore the questions
Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) uses 200 responses to examine which survey questions belong together.
Check the measures
Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) uses 365 responses to check that measurement structure.
Test the relationships
Structural equation modelling (SEM) uses the same 365 responses to examine how the measured ideas relate to one another.
entries.equationNote: The project record provides the model structure and R², but no path-coefficient or measurement-fit table. Numeric labels therefore remain limited to the supplied outputs.

entries.title: A positive view of the workshop links learning with intention.
entries.caption: Model coefficients · not percentages.
entries.source: Ladder Art Space project record; 216 valid responses; PROCESS Model 4.

inputs.label: Learning value
inputs.note: The source reports a learning-value → attitude path of 0.35. Its standardized status is not documented, so it remains labelled as a reported path.

inputs.label: Social value
inputs.note: Social experience is included in the model. The source record does not provide a separate numeric coefficient for this path.

inputs.label: Hedonic value
inputs.note: Enjoyment is the third experience dimension. It is modeled alongside learning and social value rather than assigned an invented effect size.

method: Check the questions
Check that the questions measure the intended workshop experiences and attitudes.
Examine the link
PROCESS Model 4 examines whether attitude helps connect experience value with intention to participate. This is called mediation.
Plan a real-world test
Beginner guidance is a proposed service test. Measuring actual bookings would require new data.
entries.equation: Experience value → workshop attitude → participation intention
entries.equationNote: PROCESS Model 4 includes a direct effect and an indirect effect through the mediator. The figure focuses on the mediated path; the source does not supply the direct coefficient or enough detail to multiply the two displayed paths into a confirmed indirect estimate.

entries.title: Feeling mine and feeling ours are different.
entries.caption: Proposed framework · no new sample.
entries.source: Existing psychological-ownership framework; no estimated sample or coefficients in the source record.

inputs.label: Individual ownership
inputs.note: The felt connection is personal: control and identification with a work target. Measurement needs to specify the target, such as a task, project or organization.

inputs.label: Collective ownership
inputs.note: A shared sense of ownership requires more than an individual response. The proposed study must define the group and justify how shared meaning is measured.

method: Define the work
Specify what a person or group feels connected to.
Separate mine from ours
Distinguish personal ownership from a shared sense of responsibility.
Plan a study
Collect new data to examine how these feelings relate to commitment and cooperation.
entries.equationNote: The model is a conceptual specification. Numerical coefficients remain unestimated.

entries.title: Three examples connect guest needs with service ideas.
entries.caption: Three guest needs · service concepts.
entries.source: Interpretation framework linked to the Da Nang segmentation study; no separate dataset or numerical weights.

profiles.label: Rest & comfort
profiles.theme: Room comfort, calm and service care
profiles.response: Make room readiness and a restful stay reliable.
profiles.question: Which elements of comfort do guests mention and evaluate consistently?

profiles.label: Local experience
profiles.response: Connect guests with a small set of useful local experiences.
profiles.question: Does local experience add value after basic service quality is accounted for?

profiles.label: Reliable stay
profiles.response: Reduce friction during arrival and everyday requests.
profiles.question: Which service failures repeatedly weaken value judgments?

method: Start with reviews
Use the review themes from the linked customer-grouping study.
Describe guest needs
Organize the ideas around comfort, care and local experience.
Check with guests
Interviews and a new survey could test whether these proposed needs are distinct.
entries.equation: Review theme → value dimension → service hypothesis
entries.equationNote: The profiles organize questions for service design. They are not additional observed clusters or measured market shares.
